paragraphs.title: The Invasion and the Appeal to the Lord

answers: The children of Moab and Ammon
easy.explanation: The passage says that the children of Moab and Ammon came against Jehoshaphat.
easy.q: Who came against Jehoshaphat to battle?

answers: A great multitude was coming against him
The battle had already been won
easy.explanation: Messengers told Jehoshaphat that a great multitude was coming against him.
Jehoshaphat proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.
easy.q: What did Jehoshaphat proclaim throughout Judah?

answers: He sought the LORD and proclaimed a fast
He went out alone to fight
medium.explanation: He set himself to seek the LORD and proclaimed a fast.
medium.q: What did Jehoshaphat do after hearing about the enemy?

answers: To ask help of the LORD
medium.explanation: Judah gathered together to ask help of the LORD.
medium.q: Why did the people of Judah gather together?

medium.explanation: The passage says that Hazazon-tamar was En-gedi.
medium.q: What place is identified as Hazazon-tamar?

answers: The danger concerned only the king
Seeking the LORD was a united action of the people
challenge.explanation: People came from all the cities of Judah to seek the LORD.
challenge.q: What does the gathering from all the cities of Judah show?

answers: Hearing the report, seeking the LORD and fasting, gathering
challenge.explanation: Jehoshaphat first heard the report, then sought the LORD and proclaimed a fast, and Judah gathered.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

answers: A great military threat versus dependence on the LORD
Peace in the temple versus rebellion
challenge.explanation: A great enemy multitude is answered by fasting and seeking the LORD.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in this passage?

answers: In the house of the LORD
easy.explanation: Jehoshaphat stood in the congregation in the house of the LORD.
easy.q: Where did Jehoshaphat stand when he prayed?

easy.explanation: Jehoshaphat says that the LORD rules over all the kingdoms of the heathen.
easy.q: Who rules over all the kingdoms of the heathen?

easy.explanation: He asks, “O our God, wilt thou not judge them?”
easy.q: What did Jehoshaphat ask the LORD to do?

easy.explanation: The LORD gave the land to the seed of Abraham His friend.
easy.q: Short answer: What did God give to the seed of Abraham?

answers: The land was given to the seed of Abraham
The land was given to the king of Moab
The land had been abandoned by Israel
medium.explanation: He recalls that God gave the land to the seed of Abraham.
medium.q: What connection did Jehoshaphat mention between the land and Israel?

answers: It was where the people could cry to the LORD and receive help
It was where enemy spoil was stored
It was where the enemies lived
medium.explanation: He says that when the people stand before the house and cry to God, He will hear and help.
medium.q: Why did Jehoshaphat mention the temple?

answers: A decision or punishment against the enemy
medium.explanation: Jehoshaphat asks God to judge the enemies who are attacking Judah.
medium.q: In this context, what does “judgment” refer to?

answers: God's rule, His gift of the land, and the purpose of the temple
challenge.explanation: His prayer recalls God's authority, His covenant gift of the land, and the temple as a place of prayer.
challenge.q: What does Jehoshaphat base his appeal for help on?

answers: They have no might and do not know what to do
The people are certain of an independent victory
The king does not know where the temple is
challenge.explanation: He says, “we have no might” and “neither know we what to do,” but their eyes are upon God.
challenge.q: What feeling of helplessness does Jehoshaphat express?

answers: All Judah, including little ones, wives, and children
challenge.explanation: All Judah stood before the LORD, including their little ones, wives, and children.
challenge.q: Who stood before the LORD with Jehoshaphat?

easy.explanation: The Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah.
easy.q: Upon whom did the Spirit of the LORD come?

easy.explanation: He said, “the battle is not yours, but God’s.”
easy.q: What did Jahaziel say about the battle?

easy.explanation: He told them not to be afraid or dismayed because of the great multitude.
easy.q: What did Jahaziel tell the people not to fear?

answers: Go out against the enemy and stand
medium.explanation: They were told to go out against them, set themselves, and stand still.
medium.q: What were the people commanded to do on the next day?

medium.explanation: They were told to see the salvation of the LORD with them.
medium.q: What were the people to see?

medium.explanation: To be dismayed is to become frightened or discouraged.
medium.q: What does “dismayed” mean in this passage?

answers: The people move from helplessness to receiving divine instruction and assurance
The people move from victory to defeat
The people move from peace to rebellion
challenge.explanation: Jehoshaphat expresses uncertainty, while Jahaziel gives God's command and encouragement.
challenge.q: What major change occurs between Jehoshaphat's prayer and Jahaziel's prophecy?

answers: The Levites of the Kohathites and Korhites
challenge.explanation: The Levites stood up to praise the LORD with a loud voice.
challenge.q: Who were among the first to respond after the prophecy?

answers: Bowing and worship, followed by praise
challenge.explanation: Jehoshaphat and the people worshipped, and the Levites praised the LORD.
challenge.q: Which combination describes the people's response?

easy.explanation: Jehoshaphat appointed singers to go before the army.

answers: Praise the LORD; for his mercy endureth for ever
The enemy is near the city
easy.explanation: They praised the LORD and declared that His mercy endures forever.
They found dead bodies, riches, precious jewels, and much spoil.
easy.q: What did Judah find when it came toward the multitude?

answers: The LORD set ambushments against the enemies, and they were smitten
medium.explanation: The LORD set ambushments against the enemy forces, and they were defeated.
medium.q: What happened when the people began to sing and praise?

answers: Ammon and Moab destroyed the inhabitants of Seir, then turned against one another
medium.explanation: Ammon and Moab first destroyed Seir, and then each helped to destroy another.
medium.q: How did the enemies destroy one another?

answers: A new altar was built there
The people blessed the LORD there
medium.explanation: They blessed the LORD there, so the place was called the valley of Berachah.
medium.q: Why was the place called the valley of Berachah?

answers: The enemies destroyed one another, and Judah gathered the spoil
The people surrendered and the enemy withdrew
challenge.explanation: The enemies fought one another, while Judah gathered the spoil afterward.
challenge.q: What was unusual about the way the victory was achieved?

answers: Gathering spoil, assembling in Berachah, and returning joyfully to Jerusalem
Returning to Jerusalem, gathering spoil, and entering the wilderness
Building ships, gathering spoil, and fasting
challenge.explanation: They gathered spoil for three days, assembled in the valley of Berachah, and returned with joy.
challenge.q: What was the sequence after the victory?

answers: The fear of God came upon them
challenge.explanation: The surrounding kingdoms feared God when they heard that the LORD fought against Israel's enemies.
challenge.q: How did the surrounding kingdoms respond to the victory?

easy.explanation: The passage says that Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah.
easy.q: Over which kingdom did Jehoshaphat reign?

answers: He departed from his father's way
He did that which was right in the sight of the LORD
easy.explanation: He walked in the way of Asa and did what was right in the sight of the LORD.
The high places were not taken away.
easy.q: What was not taken away during Jehoshaphat's reign?

answers: They had not prepared their hearts unto the God of their fathers
They did not return to Jerusalem
They did not gather the spoil
medium.explanation: The people had not prepared their hearts unto the God of their fathers.
medium.q: What shortcoming remained among the people?

medium.explanation: He reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem.
medium.q: How long did Jehoshaphat reign in Jerusalem?

answers: In the book of Jehu the son of Hanani
In the book of the kings of Moab
medium.explanation: The passage refers to the book of Jehu the son of Hanani and the book of the kings of Israel.
medium.q: Where were the rest of Jehoshaphat's acts written?

answers: A mainly righteous reign with remaining shortcomings
A reign unrelated to the LORD
challenge.explanation: Jehoshaphat did right, but the high places remained and the people had not fully prepared their hearts.
challenge.q: What balanced picture of Jehoshaphat's reign is given?

answers: Jehoshaphat walked in his father's way
Jehoshaphat opposed everything his father did
Jehoshaphat did not know his father
challenge.explanation: The passage says that he walked in the way of Asa his father.
challenge.q: What can be learned from comparing Jehoshaphat with Asa?

answers: The king did what was right, while the people had not prepared their hearts
The king was wicked, while the people were righteous
Both king and people are described as forsaking the LORD
challenge.explanation: Jehoshaphat is commended for doing right, but the people are criticized for their unprepared hearts.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the description of the king and the people?

paragraphs.title: The Alliance with Ahaziah and the Failed Ships

easy.explanation: Jehoshaphat joined himself with Ahaziah king of Israel.
easy.q: With whom did Jehoshaphat join himself?

answers: To carry spoil through the wilderness
easy.explanation: They made ships to go to Tarshish.
Eliezer the son of Dodavah prophesied against Jehoshaphat.

medium.explanation: The LORD broke the ships, and they could not go to Tarshish.

answers: He was a priest of the temple
medium.explanation: Ahaziah is described as one who did very wickedly.
medium.q: How is Ahaziah described in the passage?

answers: The LORD destroyed or frustrated the project
medium.explanation: The statement means that God brought the ship-building project to failure.
medium.q: What does “the LORD hath broken thy works” mean here?

answers: Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahaziah led to the LORD breaking his works
Fasting led to the building of ships
Victory led to war with Ahaziah
challenge.explanation: Eliezer connected the alliance with Ahaziah to the breaking of the ships.
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect relationship did Eliezer announce?

answers: The LORD delivered Judah in battle, but the venture with Ahaziah failed
Judah was defeated in battle, but the ships succeeded
Jehoshaphat acted alone and succeeded in both cases
challenge.explanation: The LORD gave victory over the enemy, but the alliance-based ship venture was broken.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between Jehoshaphat's victory and the ships?

answers: The prophecy of failure was fulfilled
The ships succeeded at another destination
The ships were used to gather the spoil
challenge.explanation: The ships were broken and could not go to Tarshish, fulfilling the prophet's warning.
challenge.q: What can be concluded from the ships' failure to reach Tarshish?
